# DopeDB (도프디비)

> DopeDB is an open-source database workspace where teams share access without
> sharing database credentials, and Codex or Claude works through one
> locally enforced session scoped to explicitly selected Project resources.

The hosted workspace coordinates secretless connection identity, membership,
policy, provider resources, revisions, and collaboration audit. Database traffic
still runs through the native desktop app. Each member uses a credential in their
OS store or receives a least-privilege, short-lived managed credential. Official
Codex and Claude ACP sessions are pinned to the selected workspace, account,
selected Project resource revisions, process, and local policy. Each session may
read the selected databases, BigQuery resources, and sources; at most one selected
database can be a write target. Desktop also reviews every external
`dopedb agent start` session before launching the official CLI.

## Key facts

- Product: Shared database access workspace for teams and AI agents
- Korean name: 도프디비
- Supported databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, MongoDB, and read-only Google BigQuery through the official bq CLI
- Managed providers: PlanetScale, Neon, and GCP Cloud SQL
- Platforms: macOS and Windows
- Price: Free
- Source availability: Open source
- Release stage: Alpha
- Safety model: Exact Agent authority, read-only defaults, immutable write proposals,
  exact approval, cancellation, manual transaction rollback, durable results, and
  operation receipts
- Credential model: Secretless shared templates plus member-local bindings or
  member-specific, short-lived managed leases
- Traffic model: Database queries run locally; the workspace service is not a
  database proxy

An Analysis Article shares sanitized HTML and one saved read-only query definition.
Authenticated members rerun it manually in Desktop; public HTML snapshots cannot
execute the query. A recipient-specific invitation requires sign-in and explicit
acceptance before workspace membership and read access are registered.

Current macOS releases are Developer ID signed and notarized. Windows installers
are not yet code-signed. System theme is the default; Light and Dark are available.
